reading.body:
QTS Ashburn 1 publishes 55 MW of IT capacity across two Sterling, Virginia buildings, ranking fifth among Virginia facilities that disclose power figures and representing roughly 4 percent of the state's published total.

That 55 MW accommodates between 1,375 racks at 40 kW per rack (typical for AI training) and 5,500 racks at 10 kW per rack (typical for colocation). The second building at 22280 Randolph Drive was under construction when this data was retrieved, so the final campus capacity may exceed the published figure. Virginia's data center concentration reflects the Ashburn corridor's position as a major hub, though most facilities in the state publish no power figure at all, making the true total unknown.

The facility holds LEED certification, which covers energy and environmental design of the building itself. No Uptime Institute tier rating, SOC attestation, or federal compliance designation appears on the published specification page, so none can be inferred. LEED certifies the structure, not the operational guarantees or security posture that differentiate data centers for different workloads.

Of Virginia's 326 mapped facilities in this dataset, only 19 publish a megawatt figure. This gap between mapped count and published capacity figures means the state's actual power footprint for data centers remains substantially larger and largely undisclosed.
